newsitem.title: USA: Motorola files patent suit against Qualcomm.
newsitem.headline: Motorola files patent suit against Qualcomm.

text.p: Motorola Inc. said Thursday it plans to file a patent infringement suit against Qualcomm Inc., alleging Qualcomm's Q phone copies the design of Motorola's handheld StarTAC digital cellular phone.
At the same time, San Diego, Calif.-based Qualcomm filed a lawsuit against Motorola, seeking a judgment that its products do not infringe any of Motorola's patents.

A Motorola attorney said the suit will be filed "very rapidly", or as soon as the necessary papers are prepared. He said it will seek an injunction to prevent Qualcomm from selling the phones, among other things. Motorola is still reviewing whether to ask for monetary damages, he said.

"The new Qualcommm QCM series of Code Division Multiple Access, or CDMA, digital cell phones copies the basic look, including the key design elements and functional features of Motorola's StarTAC wearable telephones," said Wolf Pavlok, senior vice president and general manager of Motorola's Pan American Cellular Subscriber Group.
Qualcomm said its complaint claims it and Motorola entered into patent and technology license agreements in 1990 that preclude Motorola from asserting infringement of the patents.

In its complaint, filed in federal court in San Diego, Qualcomm denies the Q Phone infringes any rights of Motorola and requests a judicial finding that Qualcomm's products are free of any infringement.

"Qualcomm was careful to respect the intellectual property rights of others, and in the course of designing any new product we seek to ensure that our design does not infringe the rights of any other companies," said Harvey White, Qualcomm president.
"In our development of the "Q" Phone we followed our usual practice of verifying and checking existing patents. Our lawsuit seeks judicial confirmation that our judgment was correct," White said.
Qualcomm stock closed down $3.25 at $59.375 on Nasdaq and Motorola added 87.5 cents to $58.675 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Separately, Motorola said its Asia Pacific Cellular Infrastructure Group plans to install a trial cellular network in mainland China. It will install the network for 43,000 subscribers throughout Beijing.
